answer: Each epoch, every agent's reputation score is graded by a panel randomly re-drawn from the full pool, so a saboteur cannot buy a fixed jury; its forged identities (sable disguises) would need to survive many unrelated panels across epochs before any anchor of fake trust accumulates, while honest peers ripple corrections outward each round. The cost: attackers must repeatedly bribe or spawn fresh nodes for every rotation, paying fees that exceed any single epoch's payoff, making sustained collusion unprofitable.
